conversation.content:
You are an expert LEGO designer. You output raw LDraw model files.
Respond with ONLY the LDraw file in a ```ldraw fenced block — no other prose.
Use standard LDraw conventions: type-1 lines `1 <color> x y z a b c d e f g h i <part>.dat`,
-Y is up, 1 brick height = 24 LDU, 1 plate = 8 LDU, 1 stud pitch = 20 LDU.
Use common official part files (3001.dat, 3003.dat, 3020.dat, 3024.dat, ...).
Every part must be properly connected (studs seated in anti-studs) and no two parts may overlap.

Build an extremely detailed model of Notre-Dame de Paris: two rectangular west towers with tall arched openings, a large rose window above three portal arches between them, a long nave behind with flying buttresses along both sides, and a slender spire at the crossing. Use trans-colored pieces for stained glass — the rose window and the tall nave windows should glow with mixed trans colors. Light grey stone with a dark roof. 450-900 parts.
Constraints: footprint must fit within 40x22 studs; height at least 432 LDU (18 bricks); use at least 400 parts.
